behavior: The watcher records only real deposits of the allowlisted token and survives reorgs and restarts
acceptance: On Anvil, a 5 USDC transfer (mock token) to a receive address gives a chain_transfers row detected, then confirmed once the block meets the confirm rule
A Transfer from a look-alike token contract, or to an unknown address, adds no row
After a reorg that drops the block the row is reorged; restarting the worker resumes from the cursor with no duplicate rows
notes: 2026-10-09 From F045 review: mark a transfer reorged before inserting its re-mined copy (otherwise a different log_index lets both stay live); on a reorg back to the original block (A->B->A) set the old row live again, since (chain_id, block_hash, log_index) is unique; decide how to store Arc native-coin Transfer logs (0xffff...fffe emitter), which the transfer->invoice token FK rejects. Book only confirmed transfers; the DB rejects other bookings and any change to a booked transfer.

2026-10-09 review fail by reviewer: Fail: one blocking defect. Acceptance lines pass (backend check ok; watcher tests -race -count=3 and -count=10 all pass; go mod tidy -diff clean, only go-ethereum v1.17.8 plus indirects added; must-not-change paths untouched; CI installs Foundry v1.5.1 and submodules before checks). BLOCKING (1): the watcher trusts one eth_getLogs answer, and treats a missing log as a reorg. (a) watcher.go:196-200 marks every detected row with block_number >= from that is absent from the answer as reorged, without comparing block hashes as S-4/D-45 require ('reorg checks must compare hashes the RPC returns'). If the answer is short (a load-balanced node one block behind that clamps toBlock to its head, or a provider returning [] on overload) in the scan where the row's block becomes final, the cursor moves to that finalized block (watcher.go:222-225), start() (:93-106) never rescans it (reorged rows do not hold the start back), and a canonical final deposit stays reorged forever. (b) Same cause: a deposit absent from that one answer in the scan where its block becomes final is never recorded. On Arc and Tempo finalized = latest, so every block is scanned once and a 1-block lag is enough. Reproduced in a scratch copy with an RPC proxy that answers eth_getLogs with [] once, then 3 healthy scans: TestPocLaggingLogsMissDepositForever -> 0 rows; TestPocLaggingLogsReorgFinalRowForever -> row left 'reorged'. Fix: mark a detected row reorged only when the RPC's header at its block_number has a different hash (or is missing below latest); and do not let one log answer be the last look at a block, e.g. rescan an overlap below last_finalized_block each scan (idempotent) or check the log node reached hi before advancing the cursor. Add a test with such a proxy. NON-BLOCKING: (2) watcher.go:169,177 confirm uses finalized from one call and the block hash from another; with load-balanced nodes a lagging node still on an orphan at height <= another node's finalized could pass. Consider reading header(n) and finalized in one JSON-RPC batch. (3) A->B->A works (scratch test: original row back to detected, B copy reorged) but is not tested; add a record()-level test. (4) Docs disagree: money-safety.md:23-24 says index Arc native Transfer logs for deposit times; architecture.md:83-84 says they are ignored. Update the owning doc; note for F049 that a native-only Arc payment creates no transfer row. (5) If a lagging node gives latest < finalized the cursor CHECK fails the scan (retried, noisy); rows above a lagging latest flap to reorged and back. (6) invoices() loads every invoice ever into one topic list each scan (ponytail noted). (7) chaintest.go:39-46 free-port race and no check that anvil is still running (a failed bind could connect to another anvil); chaintest.go:77 slices at LastIndex(out, '{\n') which panics with -1 if forge prints compact JSON.

2026-10-09 review fail by reviewer: Re-review of a2290a6: fail, one new blocking defect, one line to fix. Earlier finding 1 is fixed: a row becomes reorged only on a different header hash at its height, there is a 64-block rescan, and finalized and the judged headers come from one batch. lag_test.go covers it, my earlier PoCs now pass, and A->B->A is tested. Notes 2, 3, 4, 5 and 7 are fixed. go test -count=3 -race ./internal/watcher/ ok; pnpm --filter @forwend/backend test ok. BLOCKING (new): watcher.go:147 record(..., finalized, max(latest, finalized)). finalized is now read after eth_getLogs (in the headers batch, :111), so it can be above latest, the top of the scanned range. The cursor then stores last_finalized_block = finalized, and the next start (:155) is finalized+1-64. Blocks in (latest, finalized-64] are never scanned, and a deposit there is lost forever. Two cases: (a) Honest single node. On Arc or Tempo (finalized = latest, 0.5-0.6 s blocks), a scan that takes more than about 32 s (catch-up after downtime, many 2000-block calls) loses deposits mined just after latest was read. (b) A load-balanced eth_blockNumber that is more than 64 blocks behind. Before this commit, a lagging latest broke the cursor CHECK; now the cursor accepts it without an error. Reproduced in a scratch copy with an RPC proxy, then 3 normal scans: TestPocChainMovesDuringScan (transfer plus 70 blocks mined during the first eth_getLogs) -> 0 rows; TestPocLaggingLatest (eth_blockNumber answered once as deposit block - 1, 70 blocks behind) -> 0 rows. Fix, checked in scratch: record(ctx, reorged, deposits, min(finalized, latest), latest). Both PoCs and all 6 watcher tests then pass with -race. Add a test like TestPocChainMovesDuringScan. NON-BLOCKING: (1) The headers batch has no size limit: one element per distinct log block plus each detected row. Providers cap batch size; split it when needed. (2) If the chain goes back to a shorter fork while the re-mined copy's row sits above the new head, that row is not marked reorged (no header at its height). Bringing the original row back then breaks chain_transfers_live_log, and every scan fails until the chain grows past that height. This fixes itself and causes no wrong state.

2026-10-09 review pass by reviewer: Re-review of 2a03c86: pass. The blocking finding is fixed. watcher.go:151 calls record(..., min(finalized, latest), latest), so the cursor never passes what the scan read. TestChainMovingDuringAScanLosesNothing and TestLaggingLatestBlockLosesNothing cover both cases. My scratch PoCs now pass on the current code: TestPocChainMovesDuringScan, TestPocLaggingLatest, and the empty eth_getLogs miss and reorg PoCs. go test -count=3 -race ./internal/watcher/ passes, 24 of 24 (8 tests x 3). pnpm --filter @forwend/backend test passes. Earlier findings 1-5 and 7 are fixed. Leaving the shorter-fork case as is is fine: it recovers on its own and writes no wrong status. NON-BLOCKING: (1) watcher.go:261-265: with more than 99 judged blocks, later batch chunks may reach other nodes, so the one-node view of finalized plus header holds only for the first chunk. Low risk, because a wrong confirm still needs a node on an orphan below another node's finalized block. Note it for S-7. (2) lag_test.go: the proxy hook calls e.anvil.Transfer and Mine, which use t.Fatalf, from the HTTP server goroutine. If they fail there, the failure report is wrong (Fatal outside the test goroutine). Only matters when a test fails. (3) invoices() still loads every invoice into one topic list per scan (ponytail noted).

proof.1: backend: TestDepositIsDetectedThenConfirmed on Anvil: a 5 USDC MockToken transfer to a receive address is a detected row (amount, sender, block time), still detected one block short of finalized, confirmed once its block is finalized
proof.2: backend: TestOnlyTheInvoiceTokenToAReceiveAddressCounts: a look-alike MockToken (also a listed token of another invoice) sending to the receive address, and the real token sending to an unknown address, add no row; without the token check the foreign key rejects the row
proof.3: backend: TestReorgMarksTheDepositReorged (anvil_reorg -> reorged; the same signed tx mined again is a new detected row; a restarted Chain adds nothing and later confirms it), TestReorgBackToTheFirstBlock, TestLaggingNodeDoesNotLoseADeposit, TestLaggingNodeDoesNotReorgADeposit, TestChainMovingDuringAScanLosesNothing and TestLaggingLatestBlockLosesNothing (the cursor never passes what was scanned; both failed before the fix)
